messages.subject: Re: How to use build tools?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,
Maven is certainly a build tool, so you've already taken the first step by writing a Project Object Model (pom.xml)

The 'svm' function is declared in the e1071, so you will need to do two things:

1) Ensure that a JAR of e1071 is on your project's classpath. For example, by adding a <dependency> block to your pom.xml:
 <dependency>
    <groupId>org.renjin.cran</groupId>
    <artifactId>e1071</artifactId>
    <version>1.6-8-b27</version>
  </dependency>
2) Evaluate "library(e1071)" in your R code

You can read more about project setup from the documentation here:
http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/library/project-setup.html#

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Unable to load RH2GIS package
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I need to use the RH2GIS package to manipulate an H2/H2GIS database but it seems to be unavailable and I can't find it on packages.renjin.org <http://packages.renjin.org/> while the package H2 seems to work well.

On Renjin Studio I get the following message :
> Renjin 0.8.2515
> Copyright (C) 2017 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
> Copyright (C) 2017 BeDataDriven
> > library(RH2GIS)
> Error: Could not load package RH2GIS; tried org.renjin.bioconductor:RH2GIS, org.renjin.cran:RH2GIS

I found a workaround by compiling locally the Renjin DBI project <https://github.com/hannesmuehleisen/renjin-dbi>, but it's just a workaround.

Has anyone an idea how to solve that ?

Regards

Sylvain Palominos

messages.subject: Re: Unable to load RH2GIS package
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erwan,

since we have improved our C to Java bytecode compiler, we have added the DBI package from CRAN back to our repository and removed the replacement package (which includes RH2GIS) because of the name conflict. When you use Renjin's CLI, like in the Renjin Studio, you will not be able to use RH2GIS because the CLI only looks for packages in our repository. The workaround that Sylvain is currently using your best option to keep using the RH2GIS library. In the longer run, we can think of separating the packages related to the H2 database from the old replacement package and add these as new packages to our repository.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan
